answer: A bonded work vault resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit and publishes verifiable useful work before earning full rewards. New identities start with tiny limits, like seedlings on a reef, and gain trust only as completed tasks accumulate. A nebula of cheap fakes cannot shortcut this, because every identity must separately stake funds, wait out a cooling period, and do checkable work. A thousand sybils thus cost a thousand deposits plus a thousand work histories, while an honest agent pays once; misbehavior slashes the deposit, so attack cost grows with scale.
